title: Recruit and manage 2–3 design partners for Quantization Profile Library beta
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
## Summary
Recruit and actively manage 2–3 design partners for the **Quantization Profile Library (opt-in, route-level enablement)** beta. Partners will help validate: (a) route-level enable/disable workflows, (b) compatibility guardrails + safe fallback behavior, (c) observability + rollback playbooks, and (d) customer messaging/docs.

This is not a broad beta. It is a tightly scoped, high-touch program with explicit acceptance gates and an agreed rollback SLA.

## Goals
- Validate end-to-end experience for enabling a **specific quantization profile** on a **specific route** (and optionally region/deployment tier)
- Prove we can achieve meaningful **cost/token** savings on targeted model variants without unacceptable quality regression
- Validate operational readiness: dashboards, audit logs, safe fallback, and emergency kill-switch
- Collect actionable feedback to finalize GA scope and documentation

## Non-goals
- Automated per-customer profile recommendations / auto-tuning in production
- Default-on enablement across routes/models
- Expanding to >3 partners before we’ve proven rollback + guardrails in real traffic

## Target design partner profile (what we need)
**Partner must have:**
- A production (or near-prod) LLM workload with stable prompts and measurable KPIs
- Willingness to run a short A/B evaluation and then a staged traffic rollout (starting at ≤1%)
- Clear ownership: one Eng lead + one PM/ops owner on their side
- Ability to share outcome metrics and provide product feedback weekly

**Preferred workloads:**
- High token throughput (cost-sensitive) with clear latency SLOs
- Known model versions/variants (pinned) and stable route definitions

**Deployment mix target:**
- 1 partner on **Hosted API**
- 1 partner on **Dedicated**
- Optional 3rd partner primarily for **audit/RBAC/change control** validation (can be low-traffic)

## Candidate accounts (initial)
1) **Acme AI** (Hosted) – cost reduction priority; comfortable with experimentation and weekly check-ins.
2) **Northstar Search** (Dedicated) – strong perf sensitivity; good partner to validate tail latency + capacity interactions.
3) **FalconBank** (Observer / limited beta) – primary value is validating audit logging, RBAC expectations, and change controls; traffic enablement may be delayed due to security review.

## Beta entry criteria (must be true before enabling customer traffic)
- Route-level enablement available behind allowlist + RBAC checks (Console and/or API)
- Per-route dashboards available: enabled rate, fallback rate, errors, p95 latency deltas, cost/token deltas
- Rollback runbook validated internally (route disable + global kill-switch)
- Compatibility checks enforced (model/hardware/context constraints) with deterministic selection
- Evals playbook ready (baseline vs profile) and partner agrees to run it prior to >1% traffic

## Success criteria (what “beta success” means)
Partner-level success is assessed per model + route + region combination.
- **Cost:** measurable reduction in cost/token on targeted route(s) (goal: meaningful savings; final threshold per model family set by Applied ML benchmarks)
- **Quality:** no statistically significant regression on agreed prompt sets beyond policy thresholds; partner confirms acceptable output quality for their production KPIs
- **Latency:** p95 decode latency remains within partner’s SLO and does not materially regress relative to baseline for the enabled traffic slice
- **Ops:** rollback completes cleanly (route-level) within agreed time, with clear observability signals (applied vs fallback vs disabled)
- **UX:** partner can understand and operate the feature with minimal Redwood intervention (warnings, compatibility messages, and docs are adequate)

## Exit criteria (when we stop / pause)
- Any partner observes a material quality regression attributable to quantization profile enablement and we cannot mitigate quickly via profile selection/constraints
- Fallback loops / non-deterministic selection observed
- Sustained elevated fallback_rate or 5xx correlated with profile metadata/artifact retrieval

## Operating model (how we run the program)
**Cadence**
- 45-min kickoff call per partner (scope, guardrails, rollout plan, rollback SLA)
- Weekly 30-min check-in (results + next actions)
- Async updates via a shared Slack channel per partner (or shared channel with clear threading)

**Feedback loop artifacts**
- Shared doc: partner goals, routes/models targeted, rollout plan, and final decision log
- Weekly scorecard snapshot (cost/token, p95 latency, fallback_rate, error_rate, quality deltas)
- Running list of issues/requests filed back to Linear (with owners)

**Escalation + rollback**
- Primary escalation path: Support escalation lead + SRE on-call (during rollout windows)
- If regression detected: immediate route-level disable; if system-wide risk: global kill-switch
- Target rollback SLA during rollout windows: agree per partner (default: same business day; faster if canary window)

## Comms plan
**External (design partners)**
- Beta invitation email + one-page overview of what “opt-in” means, what we log, and how to roll back
- Explicit statement: profiles may change over time; partners will pin a profile version for beta and will not be silently moved
- Clear expectations: time commitment, data sharing boundaries, and success criteria

**Internal (Redwood)**
- Partner roster + current rollout stage posted weekly to #product and #eng-releases
- Single source of truth: this ticket + partner-specific notes linked in comments
- Release notes: avoid public announcement until at least 2 partners meet success criteria and docs/support playbook are ready

## Timeline (target)
- Week 1: recruit + confirm 2 partners; schedule kickoffs; identify routes/models and baseline metrics
- Week 2: run offline A/B evals; enable ≤1% traffic canary on 1 route per partner
- Week 3–4: expand traffic cautiously (per partner), iterate on warnings/docs/guardrails; capture case-study metrics

## Open questions
- Do we require a formal beta agreement / updated MSA addendum for audit log retention / feature volatility?
- What is the minimum set of Console UX needed for partners vs API-only enablement?
- Final thresholds: align with Applied ML policy on “borderline” regressions (who is final approver: Applied ML sponsor vs product lead?)

## Next steps
- Finalize partner shortlist and outreach plan (Markus)
- Confirm allowlist process + rollout windows (Connor O’Brien)
- Coordinate eval playbook walkthrough with each partner (Olivia Grant + Jonas Weber)
- Ensure partner-specific dashboards are ready and shared (Paula Mendes + Aisha Bello)
comments: 2025-02-06 (Marissa Cole): Aligned with Ava Chen on keeping beta tight (2–3 partners). Preference is 1 hosted + 1 dedicated; a 3rd can be audit/control heavy even if traffic is small.
2025-02-11 (Markus Klein): Draft outreach emails prepared for Acme AI + Northstar Search. Waiting on confirmation that kill-switch is on the release train before proposing rollout windows.

2025-02-19 (Marissa Cole): Northstar indicated dedicated latency sensitivity; requested clarity on compatibility matrix by GPU SKU and max context constraints. Capturing as feedback for docs/Console warnings.

2025-03-05 (Markus Klein): Acme kickoff complete. They will start with 1 route, pinned model variant, and 1% canary. They want a simple way to confirm per-request whether profile applied vs fallback (request id workflow).

2025-03-12 (Marissa Cole): FalconBank security review: they care most about audit logs (actor, route, before/after diff) and approvals. They may not enable traffic during beta; still valuable for change-control validation.
